source_text: Idcirco et in columba venit Spiritus sanctus: simplex animal et laetum, non felle amarum, non morsibus saevum, non unguium laceratione violentum, hospitia humana diligere, unius domus consortium nosse; cum generant, simul filios edere, cum commeant, volatibus invicem cohaerere, communi conversatione vitam suam degere, oris osculo concordiam pacis agnoscere, legem circa omnia unanimitatis implere. Haec est in Ecclesia noscenda simplicitas, haec charitas obtinenda, ut columbas dilectio fraternitatis imitetur, ut mansuetudo et lenitas agnis et ovibus aequetur. Quid facit in pectore christiano luporum feritas et canum rabies et venenum lethale serpentum et cruenta saevitia bestiarum? Gratulandum est cum tales de Ecclesia separantur, ne columbas, ne oves Christi saeva sua et venenata contagione praedentur. Cohaerere et conjungi non potest amaritudo cum dulcedine, caligo cum lumine, pluvia cum serenitate, pugna cum pace, cum foecunditate sterilitas, cum fontibus siccitas, cum tranquillitate tempestas. Nemo existimet bonos de Ecclesia posse discedere: triticum non rapit ventus, nec arborem solida radice fundatam procella subvertit; inanes paleae tempestate jactantur, invalidae arbores turbinis incursione evertuntur. Hos execratur et percutit Joannes apostolus dicens: Ex nobis exierunt, sed non fuerunt ex nobis: si enim fuissent ex nobis, mansissent utique nobiscum.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, the Holy Spirit also comes in a dove, a simple and joyful animal, not bitter with gall, not savage with bites, not violent with claw lacerations, to love human dwellings, to know the fellowship of one house; when they produce offspring, they bring forth their young together, when they travel, they cohere in flights together, they spend their life in common conversation, they recognize the concord of peace with a kiss of the mouth, they fulfill the law of unanimity in all things. This simplicity is to be recognized in the Church, this charity is to be obtained, so that the love of brotherhood may imitate doves, so that gentleness and mildness may be equal to lambs and sheep. What does the ferocity of wolves and the rabies of dogs and the lethal venom of serpents and the bloody savagery of beasts do in a Christian heart? It is to be congratulated when such people are separated from the Church, lest they devour the doves, lest they devour the sheep of Christ with their savage and venomous contagion. Bitterness cannot cohere and be joined with sweetness, darkness with light, rain with serenity, battle with peace, sterility with fertility, dryness with springs, tempest with tranquility. Let no one think that good people can depart from the Church: the wind does not carry away wheat, nor does a storm overturn a tree founded on a solid root; empty chaff is tossed about by a tempest, weak trees are uprooted by the incursion of a whirlwind. John the apostle execrates and strikes these people, saying: They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would certainly have remained with us.

pass_b_english: This is why the Holy Spirit also comes in a dove: a simple and joyful creature, not bitter with gall, not savage with bites, not violent with claw lacerations, one that loves human dwellings and knows the fellowship of a single household. When they produce offspring, they bring forth their young together; when they travel, they hold together in flight; they live their life in common fellowship; they recognize the concord of peace with a kiss of the mouth; and they fulfill the law of unanimity in all things. This simplicity is to be recognized in the Church, this charity is to be obtained, so that the love of brotherhood may imitate doves, and so that gentleness and mildness may equal lambs and sheep. What place have the ferocity of wolves, the rabies of dogs, the lethal venom of serpents, and the bloody savagery of beasts in a Christian heart? It is to be congratulated when such people are separated from the Church, lest they devour the doves and the sheep of Christ with their savage and venomous contagion. Bitterness cannot cohere and be joined with sweetness, darkness with light, rain with serenity, battle with peace, sterility with fertility, dryness with springs, or tempest with tranquility. Let no one think that good people can depart from the Church: the wind does not carry away wheat, nor does a storm overturn a tree founded on a solid root; empty chaff is tossed about by a tempest, and weak trees are uprooted by the incursion of a whirlwind. The apostle John execrates and strikes these people, saying, "They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would certainly have remained with us" (1 John 2:19).
